t: Seville grew from a Tartessian settlement into the Roman city of Hispalis, a Visigothic royal residence at times, the seat of al-Andalus until 716, the capital of the Abbadid taifa from 1023 and a twin capital of the Almohad empire from 1163.

Ferdinand III took it after a siege of fifteen months in 1248, and from 1503 its port held the monopoly of trade with the Spanish Americas, which brought it to more than a hundred thousand people in the 16th century.
Silting of the Guadalquivir and the plague of 1649 began a decline, the Casa de Contratación went to Cádiz in 1717, and the city later hosted the Ibero-American Exposition of 1929 and Expo '92.
dyk: Seville's motto NO8DO is a rebus read as the Spanish "No me ha dejado", "She has not abandoned me", with a figure eight standing for madeja, a skein of wool; according to legend Alfonso X gave it to the city after its people stayed loyal to him against his son.

Seville is taken for the Umayyad Caliphate and serves as the seat of the governor of al-Andalus until 716
A taifa kingdom ruled by the Abbadid dynasty emerges with its capital at Seville
Seville becomes the seat of the Andalusi part of the Almohad empire, a twin capital with Marrakesh
The city surrenders to Ferdinand III of Castile after fifteen months of siege
The Casa de Contratación is placed at Seville, which becomes the port of the Indies trade
A great plague, worsened by flooding, halves the population

f.founded: Its original core dates to the 8th century BCE, when the town stood on an island in the Guadalquivir. By myth Hercules, identified with the Phoenician god Melqart, founded it; the Tartessians called it Spal or Ispal, and the Romans Latinised the name as Hispalis.
f.where: On the lower reaches of the River Guadalquivir in the south-west of the Iberian Peninsula, about 80 km from the Atlantic, in Andalusia, Spain.
f.known: Roman Hispalis; the Visigothic bishops Leander and Isidore; the capital of the Abbadid taifa; Almohad capital with the Giralda and the Torre del Oro; the Casa de Contratación and the monopoly of the American trade; the plague of 1649; the painters Velázquez, Murillo and Zurbarán; the Ibero-American Exposition of 1929 and Expo '92
f.today: Seville is the capital of the autonomous community of Andalusia and of the province of Seville, and the fifth-largest city of Spain.
